system.one_liner: Interprets all Transformer parameters by projecting them into the vocabulary embedding space, then uses that view to align models and stitch them zero-shot.

content.variant_note: three titled columns, each one application of the same projection into embedding space (read out, align, stitch), each drawn as a small pipeline
content.argues: One operation, projecting weights into vocabulary space, lets researchers read parameters as tokens, align layers across independently trained models, and stitch two models zero-shot.
content.subject: Transformer weights projected into vocabulary space: read as top-k tokens, compared across models, used to stitch two models.

lessons.what_to_learn: Show one operation applied to several targets by repeating the same small pipeline motif (vector, projection box, shared-space bar, readout) in aligned rows or columns, with real readouts as the payoff. Open up the one part whose inside needs explaining with a thought-bubble cloud, and keep one colour per model through the combined model.
lessons.suits: Analysis or framework papers where one transformation or probe is applied to several objects and each use needs its own short demonstration.

evidence: we can align layers of the two instances by casting their weights into the embedding space.
in 30% of the cases, this procedure, termed stitching, results in a classifier that reaches an impressive accuracy of 70%
Zero-shot “stitching”, where representations of a fine-tuned classifier are translated through the embedding space

summary: The paper interprets all parameters of a trained Transformer by projecting them into the embedding space of vocabulary items. Figure 1 is a three-column overview of what this view enables. Parameter Interpretation: feed-forward keys and values and the attention matrices W_VO and W_QK pass through E and appear as lists of top-k tokens from real GPT-2 layers. Parameter Alignment: key vectors of two BERT instances are projected by E_A and E_B, packed into a similarity matrix, averaged into an L1-L5 heat map and matched along a diagonal. Zero-shot Stitching: a pretrained and a finetuned model are joined by a band-aid stitching layer that translates features through the embedding space, shown inside a thought-bubble cloud. Drawn as flat pastel boxes, coloured-cell vectors and pink bars under dashed dividers.
summary_zh: 论文把Transformer全部参数投影到词表嵌入空间来解读。图1分三列：参数解读（键、值和注意力矩阵经E投影后读出top-k词）、参数对齐（两个BERT的层相似度矩阵与匹配对角线）、零样本拼接（经嵌入空间翻译的创可贴式拼接层）。
notes: Prior primary kind contribution-mosaic kept; variant set to capability-cards instead of the prior fan-out; the three columns are titled but not lettered (caption says Left, Center, Right). The 7 bitmaps are the two blue funnels, the three grey gradient arrows, the dark stitching band and the black matching matrix; the heat map, band-aids and cloud are vector. Whether the heat map shows measured values or a sketch cannot be told.
